text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police arrest 69 students suspected to be members of various secret cults and recover human skull from them.
- Meteorologists ask Nigerians to conserve food and water, saying there could be drought this year going by rainfall pattern in the last five months.
- Federal government outlaws call-back telephone system through which Nigerian Telecoms has lost billions of naira.
- Six more locomotives built for Nigerian railways by China are to be delivered on Friday.
- Uncertainty surrounds on-going talks between Nigeria and Britain to lift ban imposed on each other's aircraft.
- Federal and state security chiefs begin emergency meeting in the northern city of Kaduna over recent wave of bomb blasts in the country.
- Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha suggests that West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG could form nucleus of a sub-regional peacekeeping force after its assignment in Liberia.
- Plans by Fidelity Merchant Bank to acquire Pinnacle Merchant Bank fail.
- Nigeria pays up $1.17 million dues to United Nations for this year.
- Police launch "operation flush the pirates" campaign to stop infringement of copyright laws in Nigeria.
- Representatives of the European Union meet Nigerian political party leaders in Abuja to assess the military's transition to civil rule programme.
- Outgoing chief executive of Mobil oil producing company, Jim Massey, decries "negative attitude" of United States government to Nigeria.
